lines.text: Start with one. Keep doubling, and add up one hundred numbers.
lines.caption: Start with one. Keep doubling, and add up one hundred numbers.

lines.text: The total is thirty-one digits long! <short pause> Yet we can find its remainder in our heads.
lines.caption: The total is thirty-one digits long! Yet we can find its remainder in our heads.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this one together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this one together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Add one, plus two, plus four, plus eight, and keep doubling.
lines.caption: Add one, plus two, plus four, plus eight, and keep doubling.

lines.text: The last number is ninety-nine twos multiplied together.
lines.caption: The last number is ninety-nine twos multiplied together.

lines.text: What is the remainder when this sum is divided by seven?
lines.caption: What is the remainder when this sum is divided by seven?

lines.text: Is it zero, one, two, four, or six?
lines.caption: Is it zero, one, two, four, or six?

lines.text: So what are we really looking for?
lines.caption: So what are we really looking for?

lines.text: The remainder is what's left over after taking out all the sevens.
lines.caption: The remainder is what's left over after taking out all the sevens.

lines.text: Take twenty, for example. Two sevens make fourteen, and six is left over.
lines.caption: Take twenty, for example. Two sevens make fourteen, and six is left over.

lines.text: Now let's count the terms. The little number on top is the power.
lines.caption: Now let's count the terms. The little number on top is the power.

lines.text: Going down, each power halves: four, then two, then one. So one has power zero.
lines.caption: Going down, each power halves: four, then two, then one. So one has power zero.

lines.text: So the powers go from zero up to ninety-nine.
lines.caption: So the powers go from zero up to ninety-nine.

lines.text: That's one, plus ninety-nine more. One hundred terms, not ninety-nine!
lines.caption: That's one, plus ninety-nine more. One hundred terms, not ninety-nine!

lines.text: The total is far too big to work out. We need a pattern.
lines.caption: The total is far too big to work out. We need a pattern.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our strategy: look for a pattern in the remainders.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our strategy: look for a pattern in the remainders.

lines.text: One, two and four are smaller than seven. They leave one, two and four.
lines.caption: One, two and four are smaller than seven. They leave one, two and four.

lines.text: Eight is seven plus one. So eight leaves one!
lines.caption: Eight is seven plus one. So eight leaves one!

lines.text: Sixteen is fourteen plus two. It leaves two.
lines.caption: Sixteen is fourteen plus two. It leaves two.

lines.text: Thirty-two is twenty-eight plus four. It leaves four.
lines.caption: Thirty-two is twenty-eight plus four. It leaves four.

lines.text: See the cycle? One, two, four, and then back to one.
lines.caption: See the cycle? One, two, four, and then back to one.

lines.text: Here's why. Each power is double the last, so its remainder doubles too.
lines.caption: Here's why. Each power is double the last, so its remainder doubles too.

lines.text: When it gets too big, we take out a seven. Double four is eight, and eight leaves one.
lines.caption: When it gets too big, we take out a seven. Double four is eight, and eight leaves one.

lines.text: Now add one cycle. One plus two plus four is seven. Nothing left over!
lines.caption: Now add one cycle. One plus two plus four is seven. Nothing left over!

lines.text: So let's split our hundred terms into groups of three.
lines.caption: So let's split our hundred terms into groups of three.

lines.text: Every group leaves one, two and four. That's seven, a perfect fit.
lines.caption: Every group leaves one, two and four. That's seven, a perfect fit.

lines.text: Ninety-nine terms make thirty-three groups. Together, they leave nothing.
lines.caption: Ninety-nine terms make thirty-three groups. Together, they leave nothing.

lines.text: One term is left on its own. Its power is ninety-nine.
lines.caption: One term is left on its own. Its power is ninety-nine.

lines.text: Powers zero, three, six, and so on, start a cycle. They all leave one.
lines.caption: Powers zero, three, six, and so on, start a cycle. They all leave one.

lines.text: Ninety-nine is a multiple of three. So the last term leaves one.
lines.caption: Ninety-nine is a multiple of three. So the last term leaves one.

lines.text: So the whole sum leaves a remainder of one. The answer is B!
lines.caption: So the whole sum leaves a remainder of one. The answer is B!

lines.text: Here's a clever second way. Let's add one more one to our sum.
lines.caption: Here's a clever second way. Let's add one more one to our sum.

lines.text: One plus one is two. Two plus two is four. Four plus four is eight.
lines.caption: One plus one is two. Two plus two is four. Four plus four is eight.

lines.text: It keeps snowballing, all the way to the end.
lines.caption: It keeps snowballing, all the way to the end.

lines.text: The total becomes one hundred twos multiplied together.
lines.caption: The total becomes one hundred twos multiplied together.

lines.text: So our sum is that big number, minus one.
lines.caption: So our sum is that big number, minus one.

lines.text: Now, eight leaves one. So when we only care about sevens, times eight acts like times one!
lines.caption: Now, eight leaves one. So when we only care about sevens, times eight acts like times one!

lines.text: Ninety-nine twos make thirty-three eights. So that part leaves one.
lines.caption: Ninety-nine twos make thirty-three eights. So that part leaves one.

lines.text: One more two doubles it. So one hundred twos leave two.
lines.caption: One more two doubles it. So one hundred twos leave two.

lines.text: Take away one, and the remainder is one. Same answer!
lines.caption: Take away one, and the remainder is one. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When every term doubles, this trick turns the sum into one power.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When every term doubles, this trick turns the sum into one power.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Zero is what you get with only ninety-nine terms. Don't forget the last one!
lines.caption: Zero is what you get with only ninety-nine terms. Don't forget the last one!

lines.text: Two is the remainder of the big power, before taking away one.
lines.caption: Two is the remainder of the big power, before taking away one.

lines.text: Four and six can never happen. Look at the running totals.
lines.caption: Four and six can never happen. Look at the running totals.

lines.text: One, three, seven, fifteen, thirty-one, sixty-three. They only leave one, three, or zero.
lines.caption: One, three, seven, fifteen, thirty-one, sixty-three. They only leave one, three, or zero.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Count your terms carefully, starting from power zero.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Count your terms carefully, starting from power zero.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? This time, the sum stops at power fifty.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? This time, the sum stops at power fifty.

lines.text: And we divide by five. What is the remainder?
lines.caption: And we divide by five. What is the remainder?

lines.text: Use the same plan. Find the cycle first!
lines.caption: Use the same plan. Find the cycle first!

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Divided by five, the powers leave one, two, four, three, and then one again.
lines.caption: Let's check. Divided by five, the powers leave one, two, four, three, and then one again.

lines.text: This cycle is four long. One plus two plus four plus three is ten. That's two fives!
lines.caption: This cycle is four long. One plus two plus four plus three is ten. That's two fives!

lines.text: From power zero to power fifty, there are fifty-one terms.
lines.caption: From power zero to power fifty, there are fifty-one terms.

lines.text: Fifty-one is twelve fours, plus three. So forty-eight terms make twelve full groups. They leave nothing.
lines.caption: Fifty-one is twelve fours, plus three. So forty-eight terms make twelve full groups. They leave nothing.

lines.text: Three terms are left over, with powers forty-eight, forty-nine and fifty.
lines.caption: Three terms are left over, with powers forty-eight, forty-nine and fifty.

lines.text: Forty-eight is a multiple of four, so power forty-eight starts a new cycle.
lines.caption: Forty-eight is a multiple of four, so power forty-eight starts a new cycle.

lines.text: They leave one, two and four. That adds up to seven, and seven leaves two!
lines.caption: They leave one, two and four. That adds up to seven, and seven leaves two!

lines.text: If you found a remainder of two, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found a remainder of two, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Find the cycle of remainders. Check if one full cycle adds up to a multiple of the divisor.
lines.caption: Find the cycle of remainders. Check if one full cycle adds up to a multiple of the divisor.

lines.text: Then deal with the leftover terms.
lines.caption: Then deal with the leftover terms.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep spotting patterns, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep spotting patterns, and I'll see you next time!
